newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa heads lower as rally pauses.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa heads lower as rally pauses.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures stayed lower by the close on Wednesday on trade profit-taking, stalling a rally that lifted the market to 12-month high earlier this week.
But traders said it was difficult to draw a conclusion from today's setback as activity was less robust and centred on a few players.
"It was a very quiet and dull affair," said one.
Volume was 8,663 lots, inflated partly by AA trades.
The market started a shade higher. It reversed direction to stay in the minus column throughout the day and disappointed the bulls who had expected to see much higher prices.
New York cocoa futures also corrected lower after hitting a nine-year high on Tuesday.
Benchmark September was 10 stg down at 1,136 stg a tonne after a high of 1,150. The contract hit a one-year high of 1,162 on Tuesday.
December was seven stg lower at 1,140.
While the overall technical outlook remains buoyant, traders said the run-up was not matched by solid fundamentals.
"Fundamentally, it is trading on a flimsy foundation," said one.
The dry spell expected later this year following the El Nino weather may affect the crop in the longer term but in the immediate term, West Africa is receiving above average rainfall.
"This is why people call it a silly season...this is the time prices go up," the trader said.
Another said: "But in a silly season, anything is possible."
